scenes.headline: How one binary runs 52 diffusion models
scenes.sub: Text encoder, denoiser and decoder, each one a ggml graph
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Damson! One small C++ program runs dozens of image and video models, with no Python.

scenes.text: The model is recognised from its tensor names and sized from their shapes, and every part runs as a graph on any backend.
scenes.say: The idea: recognise a model from its tensor names, size it from their shapes, and run every part as a graph.

scenes.title: A pipeline, as the code runs it

steps.say: It reads the checkpoint's tensor names first. A prefix like double blocks means Flux.
The prompt goes through the text encoder, which for recent models is a whole language model.
The denoiser, a U-Net or a DiT, is built as a graph and run on the chosen device.

steps.note: Guidance at 1.0 skips the second pass
steps.say: The sampler loop is plain C++ on the host. Each step calls the graph once, or twice with guidance on.
Then the image decoder turns the final latent into pixels.

scenes.title: What a weight type actually converts
scenes.say: Four rules decide what a weight type converts.

items.say: Linear layers take the type you ask for, if their rows fit its blocks.
Embeddings keep the file's own type.

scenes.label: of the SD 1.5 UNet is convolution weights, which never quantise
scenes.note: q4_0 takes the whole pipeline from 2.06 to 1.59 GiB
scenes.say: So sixty-eight and a half percent of the Stable Diffusion one point five U-Net never quantises.

scenes.title: What flash attention saves
scenes.text: heads x L x L x 4 bytes

parts.say: Without flash attention, every head writes a full score matrix.
Every token scored against every token.
In thirty-two-bit floats, that is exactly six hundred mebibytes for Flux at seven sixty-eight pixels.

scenes.title: The docs' own memory table
scenes.credit: the project's docs; its memory figures

steps.say: The project's own Flux table. The memory under each type is the denoiser's weights, nothing else.
At the smallest type the cat changes colour and the sign misspells itself.

scenes.text: Weight types apply to matrices, not to models. Know which parts are convolutions before you pick a file.
scenes.say: So: weight types apply to matrices, not to models.

recap: Model found from its tensor names
Sampler on the host, one graph per call
Convolutions stay f16 at every type
scenes.say: To recap: models found by tensor name, a host-side sampler, and convolutions that never quantise.
